note: Clean pass with three disclosed caveats. (1) The study's own deposit (PLOS S1 File, an SPSS .sav) carries NO variable labels and NO value labels on any of its 130 columns, and the paper reproduces no items, so the wording is the canonical Chinese SSRS (肖水源 1986-1993) taken from a circulating full-text copy of the instrument (cdn.xuansiwei.com/t14922685/1650104979830/4、shehuizhichipingdingliangbiao.pdf), not from this study's materials. (2) Items 5, 6 and 7 are composite scores, not single choices: S5 is the sum over five family sources each rated 无/极少/一般/全力支持 (observed 10-20, consistent with 5 sources x 1-4), and S6/S7 are counts of endorsed support sources (observed 1-5 and 3-7). Their response formats have no per-level labels, so option_text is blank for all 21 of those rows and the multi-part response format is carried inside item_text instead, which is the only place it can attach. Note the circulating scoring rule says item 5 sums 'A、B、C、D四项' while its own item lists five sub-items A-E; the data (max 20) show five. (3) The English in the *_translated columns was produced by this project (translation_source=machine_translation), which owes a line on the public issues page. Mapping is PARTIAL, not VERIFIED -- see verification_liu_2017_ssrs_support.csv: the deposit's own subscale columns pin subscale membership exactly, but S1/S3/S4, S8/S9/S10 and S6/S7 are not separated within their groups by any structural route. No rights restriction on the SSRS wording was found to quote; the instrument is reproduced freely in the Chinese literature. AUDIT WARN EXPLAINED (orchestrator, Step 5c): audit_batch.R WARNs '42.9% of rows have blank option_text | 3 of 10 items have NO option_text rows (S5, S6, S7)'. This is a property of the instrument, NOT an itemtext defect and NOT a response-data defect. SSRS items 5-7 are not Likert items: item 5 is a 5-source support matrix scored 1-4 per source and summed (observed range 10-20 in this sample), items 6 and 7 are counts of support sources (observed 1-5 and 3-7). None of those levels carries a published label, so per the standing rule option_text is left blank rather than padded with the level number, and the multi-part response format is carried inside item_text. Verified per-item against the shipped file: S1-S4 and S8-S10 are 1-4 (7 items x 4 = 28 labelled rows), S5 is 10-20 (11 rows), S6 is 1-5 (5), S7 is 3-7 (5) -- 21 blank of 49 = 42.9%, exactly the WARN. The 1-7 / 10-20 union that validate_items.R reports is the union of those three composites with the seven Likert items. No issue to file.

Clean pass with two caveats. (1) ADMINISTERED LANGUAGE NOT RECOVERABLE: the study ran in Chinese (208 working adults in Shanghai recruited via WeChat), but neither the PLOS article nor its supporting information (S1 Table = the S2 XLSX deposit, S1 Fig, S1 Protocol) carries any Chinese item wording -- the workbook's headers are bare codes Optimism1..Optimism10 with no variable or value labels -- so the English original ships in the base fields under the text_source=translated_substitute fallback, language=Chinese, _translated columns empty. (2) REVERSE-CODED ITEMS: S1 Table's caption states 'All reverse variables have been reverse coded', and the data confirm it (alpha of the six scored items as stored = 0.645, matching the paper's published .65; un-reversing 3/7/9 drops it to 0.093), so option_text for Optimism3/7/9 is reversed to 1 = strongly agree .. 5 = strongly disagree while the other seven carry the paper's stated 1 = strongly disagree .. 5 = strongly agree. Mapping status is PARTIAL, not VERIFIED: the evidence pins the scored six {1,3,4,7,9,10} and the filler four {2,5,6,8} to canonical LOT-R positions and each scored item to a polarity class, but nothing distinguishes Optimism1 from 4 from 10, Optimism3 from 7 from 9, or the four fillers from one another. No rights restriction was found on the LOT-R wording; Carver's instrument page (local.psy.miami.edu) is unreachable from this sandbox (curl exit 000), so nothing was quotable either way, and per the 'silence is permission' rule the wording ships.
